_doc: Data layers this job aggregates, and how the merge resolves them. The three layers are COMPLEMENTARY (different columns), not three views of the same field — so the merge uses per-field AUTHORITY (source-of-truth ranking), not 2-of-3 consensus. Every source's value is kept in _provenance.json; a row's `conflicts` column lists any field where 2+ sources gave differing non-null values beyond tolerance.

layers.name: Redfin Data Center
layers.notes: Public S3 TSV of monthly market aggregates per zip. Fills market.csv. Answers 'how each neighborhood moved up/down'. No per-property rows.

layers.name: NJ public records (MOD-IV / SR1A deed sales)
layers.notes: Statewide maps.nj.gov MOD-IV Cadastral layer, queried per (COUNTY, MUN_NAME) from nj_municipalities.json (ZIP5 in the data is dirty). Authoritative sold price + date; best-effort sqft/garage from BLDG_DESC. Residential (class 2) only; drops SR1A non-usable deed codes. NO days-on-market, list price, beds/baths, or amenities (those come from listing_scrape). Holds the most-recent sale per parcel, so a home that sold twice in the window shows once.

layers.name: Listing scrape (Redfin / Realtor / Zillow)
layers.notes: Per-house listing detail incl. DOM, price-cut timeline, amenities. Only reliable for RECENT listings; scrape-gated (403s datacenter IPs) so MUST run locally. Reuses house-hunt's HomeHarvest path. TODO.

field_authority._doc: Per field, ordered list of source keys. Merge fills the column from the FIRST listed source that has a non-null value. Fields with one source just list that source.

conflict_tolerance._doc: For numeric fields, sources within this relative tolerance are NOT flagged as conflicting. sold_price 2% apart is rounding; 20% apart is a real disagreement worth the `conflicts` flag.
